question.leadin: The Battle of Las Navas de Tolosa paved the way for successful later sieges of Cordoba and Seville in this conflict.
question.text: Name this religious conflict between Christian states and Muslim states in the Iberian Peninsula, which is named for the reacquisition of traditionally Christian lands.
question.clue: It is often held to have begun at Covadonga and was completed with expulsion of the Nasrids under Boabdil and the destruction of al-Andalus.

swap.leadin: This person names an "exchange" that transferred plants, animals, and diseases between Europe and the Americas.
swap.text: Name this Genoese explorer, who "discovered" the New World in 1492 with the ships Nina [NEEN-yah], Pinta, and Santa Maria.
swap.clue: After landing on the island of Guanahani, he took several Arawak natives captive and renamed the island San Salvador.

question.text: This confessor of Isabella also led the the Spanish Inquisition as the Grand Inquisitor.
question.clue: This Dominican friar was the first Grand Inquisitor, becoming infamous for his zeal and cruelty.

swap.leadin: This fleet attempted to meet with the troops of the Duke of Parma but, while waiting at Gravelines, was attacked by the British navy and was forced to go north.
swap.text: Identify this fleet that King Philip II of Spain sent to conquer England in 1588.
swap.answerHtml: the Spanish Armada [accept Grande y Felicisima Armada or Armada Invencible]
swap.clue: The plan was for this force to join with one under Alessandro Farnese, but before that could happen, it participated in its first engagement off Eddystone.

question.leadin: After Jose Sanjurjo died in a plane crash, this man's connections with Hitler and Mussolini allowed him to become Generalisimo and Head of State.
question.text: Name this man, who served as dictator of Spain after winning the Spanish Civil War.
question.clue: This leader created an air bridge using Junker-52s to deploy his Army of Africa in a coup against Manuel Azana's Popular Front.

swap.leadin: Answer the following about the Ninth Crusade.
swap.text: There was another Crusade after the Ninth: one led by Peter III, king of this Spanish region. King Ferdinand, from this region, married Isabella of Castile.
swap.clue: This polity conquered Sicily in the wake of the Sicilian Vespers Uprising in 1282 during the reign of its "Great" king, Peter III.

question.leadin: Louis XIV got France into a lot of wars.
question.text: Louis's last war, this conflict was precipitated by the death of Charles II, and saw the end of French hegemony in Europe. It was concluded with the Treaty of Utrecht.
question.clue: One of the principal commanders during this war was married to Sarah Jennings, who fought battles at Oudenarde and Ramillies.

swap.leadin: Trace the path of a Carthaginian soldier in the Punic Wars.
swap.text: One of Carthage's elite slingers, our soldier hails from this island group off the coast of Spain composed of Mallorca, Menorca, and Ibiza.
swap.clue: The Carthagianians named a city in this region, Mahon, after Hannibal's brother Mago Barca. These islands, including Ibiza and Formentera, were known for their ancient slingers.

question.text: The physician Abu al-Qasim did pioneering work on dissections and removing bladder stones in this city. Abd ar-Rahman III ruled from this city, whose massive Great Mosque contained a Court of the Oranges and was converted to a Catholic cathedral in 1236.
question.clue: Mozarabs like Paul Alvar and Eulogius were hanged in this city during its namesake "Martyrs Movement."

swap.leadin: During his period of imprisonment this party derisively nicknamed his founder "the Absent One," or el Ausente.
swap.text: Name this spectrum of movements and political parties founded by Jose Antonio Primo de Rivera, and named for an ancient military formation.
swap.answerHtml: Falange [or Falange Espanola (es-PAN-yola) de la JONS; or FE de las JONS; accept word forms, such as Falangists]
swap.clue: Two leaders of this party were buried within the Santa Cruz Basilica at the Valley of the Fallen.

question.leadin: This faction was merged into the FET y de las JONS ("FET ee deh las HONS") in 1937.
question.text: Name this faction that formed as a coalition between right-leaning groups including the Falange and the Carlists. This faction opposed the Republicans in the Spanish Civil War.

swap.text: Cod was also essential for this ethnic group, whose members dominated the whaling industry from settlements by the Ebro. In 1615, Icelandic sailors killed a group of them in the so-called "Slaying of the Spaniards."
swap.clue: This ethnic group's whaling activities led to the creation of a pidgin described by Jon Olafsson, and 32 shipwrecked members of this ethnic group were murdered in Iceland in the 1615 "Slaying of the Spaniards."

question.leadin: Ringtones featuring this person's voice became popular after he interrupted Hugo Chavez, asking him, "Why don't you shut up?"
question.text: Name this ruler of Spain from 1975 to 2014, when he abdicated in favor of his son Felipe VI. This ruler oversaw the Spanish transition to democracy.
question.clue: This head of state asked Hugo Chavez "Why don't you shut up?" at a meeting where Chavez repeatedly interrupted one of his countrymen.

swap.leadin: Answer some questions about the spread of Calvinism out of its birthplace in Switzerland.
swap.text: Jeanne d'Albret, a queen of this non-French kingdom, also publicly converted to Calvinism and declared it the state religion in 1560; her son would later claim that "Paris is well worth a mass" when converting to Catholicism.
swap.clue: Another ruler of this kingdom was offered the French crown by Etienne Marcel during the Jacquerie.

question.text: Philip II's son, Philip III, expelled these people from Spain in 1609. These people were descendants of Muslims who had converted to Catholicism, and they rose up in revolt during the Rebellion of the Alpujarras.
question.clue: This silk trade-controlling group created the maritime Republic of Sale (SAL-ay), and unsuccessfully sought aid from the Huguenot stronghold of Bearn.

swap.text: This was the only city to remain in rebellion after the execution of Maldonado, Bravo, and Padilla. Padilla's wife, Maria Pacheco, led this city's defense for six more months until negotiating a peaceful surrender.
swap.clue: At this city's third council, the term filioque was incorporated into the Niceno-Constantinopolitan Creed for the first time in Western Christianity.

question.leadin: The GAL, or Antiterrorist Liberation Groups, targeted this organization in the Monbar Hotel attack.
question.text: The newspaper The World exposed a PSOE leader's involvement in death squads targeting what organization? This organization's symbol was an axe with a snake around it, and it had the motto "Keep up in both."
question.answerHtml: ETA [or Euskadi Ta Askatasuna or Basque Homeland and Liberty or Basque Country and Freedom; prompt on Basque separatists]
question.clue: Members of this organization were prosecuted in the Burgos trials.

swap.text: In a later campaign, the Black Prince defeated Henry of Trastamara at this 1367 battle named for a small Spanish town, fighting on behalf of Peter the Cruel during the Civil War of Castile.
swap.clue: This 1367 clash during the Castilian Civil War, won by Pedro the Cruel thanks to English support led by a pair of brothers including John of Gaunt.

question.leadin: This man's prime minister was Antonio Canovas del Castillo, and he took power following Arsenio Martinez-Campos proclaimed him king at Sagunto.
question.text: Name this Spanish king, who took power after the fall of the first Spanish republic.
question.clue: This man, who spent part of his time in exile attending Sandhurst College, returned to Spain and was proclaimed king following the overthrow of the First Spanish Republic. Antonio Canovas de Castillo promulgated the royalist constitution during this monarch's reign in 1876.

swap.leadin: It was ended by the Treaty of the Hague.
swap.text: Identify this conflict between Philip V of Spain and France, England, the Netherlands and Austria who felt that Spain should pony up more funds for sucking it hard during War of Spanish Succession.
swap.clue: The most important military victory of this war was won by George Byng in the Battle of Cape Passaro.
